newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bourse seen rising temporarily on new fund.
newsitem.headline: Thai bourse seen rising temporarily on new fund.

text.p: Troubled Thai stocks, which have tested three-year lows recently, surged over three percent in late trading on expectations that a new government fund would prop up the market next week, analysts said on Thursday.
Encouraged by news of the fresh fund, the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) index continued a recovery that began on Wednesday following nine days of straight losses.

In late trading, it was up 30.05 points or 3.02 percent at 1,026.21. The index had tumbled to 982.03 points on Tuesday, well below the key psychological level of 1,000 and its lowest close since September 30, 1993.

The market has suffered from forced selling by brokerages of shares held by investors unable to maintain their collatoralised margins. The margins had been agreed to by the brokers when the investors first took out the loans.

To help prevent further large drops in the index, the Finance Ministry on Wednesday said it had asked the state-run Government Savings Bank to set up a 10 billion baht ($400 million) fund to be used to buy stocks and prop up the market.
The fund, which aims to purchase stocks that brokerages have had to sell, will be available from Monday.
"The fund is good as it won't interfere with the market's mechanism and at the same time will take away selling pressure from retail investors," said Susheel Narula, an analyst at Seamico Securities.

The 10-billion-baht fund is the second to attempt to revive the market. A 15.7-billion-baht fund was set up by commercial bankers and brokers in August and first entered the market last Friday. It was originally sized at 21 billion baht.
But Bumnan Liumsuwan, an analyst at Asia Credit, said both funds would provide only a short-term boost to the market.
Lack of confidence in the Thai government's stability and fears over the health of the economy were likely to renew selling by foreign investors, he said.
"What we need now is a new government which can work more efficiently and...tackle problems better than the present government of Prime Minister Banharn (Silpa-archa)," he said.
Analysts said investors were closely watching to see what the prime minister would do after a censure debate next week in parliament.
The opposition has tabled a no-confidence motion against Banharn, and debate will begin on September 18. Among other things, the motion accuses him of economic mismanagement.
Some vocal members of Banharn's six-party coalition have urged him to quit or hand over his job to a senior politician.

"The political scene is expected to become clearer about one month after the no-confidence debate, and the market should become more stable with the index moving between 1,000-1,100 points," Susheel added.
